source.title: CURTAIN: Towards a Foundation Model for Neutrino Telescopes
source.authors: S. Magel; Felix J. Yu; C. Argüelles

record.tranche_reason: Applies pretraining-data scaling measurements to a simulated neutrino-event SSL task, a non-text modality and training regime; it reports held-out pretraining loss and downstream performance as pretraining set size changes.
record.gate_note: The study reports query AUCs and comparisons with Neptune and PolarBERT, but those results do not measure the claim versions catalogued here. It cites Kaplan et al.; it does not test language-model parameter or compute scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps pretraining set size (100k to 3.9M simulated neutrino events) at a fixed 2.2M-parameter encoder. It reports held-out SSL loss and downstream reconstruction error at each size, so it is a new-modality setting with results on V5 and V6. It fits no power law and has only four sizes from single runs, so it is a weak test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CURTAIN's pretext loss and both downstream tasks improve monotonically with pretraining set size, and that it transfers across geometry and beats from-scratch training and the other SSL baselines. In the abstract they call the monotone improvement 'as predicted by scaling laws' without fitting one. They leave model-size and compute-constrained scaling laws for future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fixed-size SSL data-scaling sweep on simulated neutrino events, not a language-model scaling-law fit; it varies event count and reports loss and downstream reconstruction metrics, without fitting exponents or testing compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Pretraining event-set size changes the reported losses and downstream metrics. Cross-geometry performance also depends on the pretraining-set size.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 workshop, as stated in the paper
record.problems: All reported values come from single training runs, with no estimate of run-to-run variation. Results use simulation with simplified detector components and medium; the study does not fit a power law.
record.rows_left_out: Intermediate plotted values for the sweeps are not stated in the text and were not read off the figures. Query AUC results and comparisons with Neptune and PolarBERT are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions here.

untested.parts: Whether the loss follows a power-law form: no fit, only four data sizes, no model-size or compute axis.
Quantitative prediction of downstream performance from scale or from pretraining loss; model-size scaling.
Extrapolation from small to larger runs.
Fitting choices and disagreement between fitted exponents.

missing.what: Neptune baseline: downstream performance does not improve with pretraining set size
PolarBERT baseline: energy error improves with data (draws level with from-scratch at 500k, overtakes it from 1M); direction stays far behind from-scratch (7.17° at best)

record.verdict_notes: Scaling is a secondary property check in a methods paper. All values come from single runs with no uncertainty. The loss drop is small (about 2.7%) over 39x more data. The rows on single sweep points (r2, r4, r6, r7) are better treated as parts of the sweeps than as separate results.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on smaller runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture changes at fixed parameter count.

The study varies pretraining event count at fixed encoder size, but does not fit or establish a power-law form; it does not test image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer loss curves as power laws.

It reports downstream metrics against pretraining event count, not a quantitative prediction from pretraining loss or a fitted scaling law; it studies neutrino reconstruction tasks rather than language-model downstream tasks.
Fit choices, exponent disagreements, and departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: CURTAIN-pretrained DeepIce encoder
rows.size_stated: 2.2 million encoder parameters; 2.5 million parameters during pretraining including the query head
rows.operation_detail: Measured held-out SSL loss across pretraining event-set sizes.
rows.value: Falls monotonically from 0.585 at 100 thousand events to 0.569 at 3.9 million events.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend as consistent with data scaling at fixed model size, but does not fit or report a power law.
rows.check: The loss falls monotonically (0.585 to 0.569) over about 1.6 orders of magnitude of data. With four points, no fit and no stated functional form, the row cannot show whether a power law holds. A monotone fall alone does not establish the version's power-law form.
